chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abu al-Hasan al-Hadda, said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say to Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq: 'What prevented you from performing Hajj?' He replied: 'Suretyship (guaranteeing a debt) that I undertook.' He said: 'What do you have to do with suretyships? Do you not know that suretyship is what destroyed the previous nations?'

key_terms.كَفَالَة: Suretyship or guaranteeing a debt/obligation for another

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq advise against getting involved in suretyship (kafalah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the distraction of *kafalah* (financial suretyship) from the obligatory pilgrimage, linking it to the moral decay that destroyed previous nations. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on prioritizing spiritual duties over social entanglements, warning that excessive involvement in others' affairs can lead to negligence of one's own religious obligations.
